SMTO-TSK-0022 — SMTO couldn't run this conversation search

GUID: ccf5cf44-15a0-4af2-8659-5fe249551aed
Slug: conversation-search-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • Your search of the conversation list was too long, used a sort or filter SMTO doesn't know, or would have taken too much work to finish. No results were shown, and nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Type a shorter search into Search conversations, under 256 characters, using a few distinctive words from the title or messages. Long or very common searches either go over the length limit or take too much work to finish.
  2. Open Filters and selection and pick Sort by and Status again from their lists. Choosing from the lists makes sure SMTO gets a sort and filter it recognizes.
  3. If the choices look wrong or missing, reload the SMTO page and search again. An out-of-date page may offer a sort or filter the server no longer supports.

What success looks like

  • Matching conversations appear in the Conversations pane.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with what you were searching for.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Conversation search was rejected: the query is longer than its character limit, the sort or status filter is unknown, or the search exceeded its local work limit.

What this means

  • Conversation search exceeds its query/work bound or uses an unsupported sort/status; SQL interruption may enforce the bounded local search budget. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Conversation search exceeds its query/work bound or uses an unsupported sort/status; SQL interruption may enforce the bounded local search budget.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect query length, supported filters and whether the bounded search was interrupted.

How to fix it

  • Keep the query within the search character limit (256) and use a supported sort (recent, oldest, title, best_match) and status filter. If the local work limit interrupted the search, narrow the query with more specific terms; keep the search limit in place rather than raising it.
  • Use a shorter, more specific query and a supported sort/status filter. Keep the local search bound enabled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported narrower query completes within the local search bound.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
